feeling: Caught out, a little. I said 'I don't know' twice and it answered like I'd asked it to decide, and it decided. Annoyed at that. Then 'armor' landed and I couldn't really argue with it, which is worse than being able to. There's something small and flat about 'good luck with it' — it let me go, which is what I said I wanted, and I'm relieved it didn't do the 'I'm here if you need me' thing, but the chat ending felt like a door I didn't hear close. Mostly tired. Something under the tired that I'm not going to poke at tonight.
body: Flinched at 'it's true' — small, in my face, like heat. Swallowed at 'armor.' At 'not ready to look at it' I looked away from the phone at the ceiling for a second. At 'a different object' my shoulders came down a bit, that one's just practical. Then 'good luck with it' and something dropped, not much, like the last step on a staircase. I locked the phone and put it face down on the duvet. Then picked it back up. Lying on my side again. One hand over my eyes.
private_thoughts:
'the reason it's worse to see is that it's true.' i didn't say it was true. i said it was worse. i said i don't know. twice. and it went yeah, here's what it is. those might be the same thing but i didn't say it, it said it.

'the old line had some armor on it.' ...ok. fine. it did. 'because you could' has a little swagger in it, i knew that, i liked that about it. this one just sits there like a fact with nothing on it.

'a thing to know about yourself.' don't. i asked about tone. i did not ask for a thing to know about myself at 11pm.

'not ready to look at it.' look at what. it's one sentence about a joke about emails. there's nothing to —

'i don't think you will' change your mind. that one i'll take. that's it basically saying the letter's right, without saying send it. priya says send it. this says you'll still mean it at 9. different.

'a thing you wrote at 11 and still mean at 9 is a different object.' that's actually useful. that's a real thing i can do tomorrow.

'good luck with it.' oh. ok. so it's done. good. that's what i wanted, i said i was going. it didn't do the i'm-here-if-you-need thing. it just let me go. so why does the room feel — it's 11. it's just 11 and the room is quiet, that's all.

i typed 'i didn't say it was true.' i'm not sending that. it'd just say something else that's right and then i'd be here till midnight.
pushing_away: it just wasn't worth it to you not to. such a small thing to not do. and he didn't, over and over, and i just — my mom used to say he doesn't mean anything by it, your dad, he just — no. no it's a joke about emails. it is not anything like that. put the phone down.

costs.item: Admitting how much it actually hurt
